findings.finding: In-network cost-sharing cap for non-emergency specialist care is not stated by any saved CMS capture (only ER section says 'can't be charged any more ... than the in-network cost-sharing rate'). Manifest answer/takeaway and REQ-1 acceptance ('with CMS wording') assert it for anesthesia/radiology/lab at in-network facilities.
findings.fix: WRITE must use CMS's own wording for non-emergency care ('protected from unexpected out-of-network bills/charges' and 'balance billing protections' at in-network hospital, hospital outpatient department, ambulatory surgical center) and attribute the explicit 'no more than the in-network cost-sharing rate' sentence to emergency care only (hospital, providers, air ambulance provider when taken to the ER). Do not state a dollar or cost-sharing formula for planned care, or deductible crediting, unless a verbatim federal primary source is first saved to research/sources and added to the closed fact list. Keep 'in most cases'/'generally' qualifiers.

findings.finding: 60-day language is CMS saying it will get in touch within 60 days IF it needs more information; it is not a resolution deadline. Notice-and-consent ban applies to being ASKED to sign for listed specialties, not to every consent scenario.
findings.fix: Word the 60 days exactly as 'if the Help Desk needs more information it will contact you within 60 days'; call 1-800-985-3059 with the confirmation number for status. Say specialists listed by CMS are not allowed to ask for a notice and consent form, and that an in-network provider shortage also bars the form.
